chapter: Records, dances and Blanche Calloway (repeated passages)
title: Miff Mole, Teagarden and Jimmy Harrison
summary: Black and white players traded ideas; Miff Mole was the talk of the music world, and Teagarden and Harrison took their approach from Louis.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: No. The Colored guys used to like that. They tried to play that way, too, just like the White boys tried to play like the Colored guys. They both traded things, you know. And at the time... Miff Mole was great at that time, you know?
Yes, I did. All trombone players liked him! Yeah. Miff Mole was the talk of the music world.
And when Teagarden and Jimmy Harrison came along, was that kind of like a different style?
It was a different type of... It was on a Louis Armstrong type, you know. Louis would have been (?) with these guys. They got their approach(?) from Louis.
